answer: PostgreSQL was chosen for billing because auditability mattered more than migration effort. DynamoDB was tried for the billing prototype but the migration failed because conditional-update semantics did not match the transaction flow; the failure was later confirmed after reviewing integration-test output.

Redis caching was tested to reduce API latency, then abandoned because it increased cache invalidation complexity. It was later retried with a narrower cache scope, but the latency improvement was negligible.

The first invoice export attempt timed out after 18 minutes. Exports were then switched to asynchronous jobs. The first full customer batch subsequently completed successfully via the asynchronous approach.

Webhook migration moved from polling to webhooks after the provider fixed signature verification. Webhooks were later temporarily disabled because duplicate deliveries caused reconciliation errors, then re-enabled after idempotency handling was deployed. Latest known state: webhooks enabled/active.
